turns.t: Hi there, I'm Dr. Hanley. Before anything, can you tell me your full name so I know I've got the right chart?
Luis Delgado.
Mr. Delgado, perfect, that matches. What brought you in tonight?
Probably nothing. My neck's been stiff, and my wife made me come.
Your wife made you come, and your neck is stiff. How long has the stiff neck been going on?
Since Sunday. So two days.
Two days. Is it worse when you move, or all the time?
When I look down, mostly. Like trying to tie my shoes.
Okay, worse looking down. Does bright light bother your eyes?
Not really. Well, the lamp at home, no.
So the light isn't bothering you. Have you been throwing up?
Nope.
Good. Have you taken anything for it?
Tylenol, 500 mg. Every six hours. And some ibuprofen, 200 mg, I took two doses since yesterday.
Tylenol 500 mg every six hours, and ibuprofen 200 mg, twice. Thanks, that helps me know what's in your system.
I'm fine, honestly. I should be at work.
What do you do for work?
I'm a roofer. Got a job on the east side I'm already behind on.
A roofer, so lots of ladders. Let me check your numbers now. Give me your arm, please.
Temperature is 39.4 °C. Heart rate is 112. And blood pressure is 118/72.
Is that bad? I felt warm in the truck, I figured it was the heater.
Your temperature is high, Mr. Delgado, 39.4. I want to be straight with you, that's a real fever, and I'm taking it seriously.
Huh. All right.
Any allergies to medicines or anything else I should know about?
No allergies. Never had one.
No allergies, thank you. Now I'm going to move your head a little. Let me know if it's sore.
Sure.
I'm bringing your chin toward your chest now. Does that hurt?
Yeah, that's tight. Pulling right down my neck.
Your neck is stiff when I bend your head forward. And I'm looking at your skin, your arms and chest, and it's clear. No rash anywhere.
Okay. That's good, right?
The skin is good news. Let me ask about the rest of you. Any trouble with your thinking, your speech, feeling confused, or weakness?
Nothing like that. I'm normal in my head.
Okay, that's reassuring. So, here is what happens next. I'm ordering blood cultures right now, the nurse will draw them.
Okay. Is that necessary?
Yes. Fever with a stiff neck is something we check carefully, not something we guess at.
Fine, whatever you need.
And I'd also like to do a lumbar puncture, which is a sample of the fluid around your spine, with a small needle in your lower back.
Sounds unpleasant.
It's uncomfortable for a few minutes, and we numb the area first. It gives us very useful information.
Okay. I trust you.
Thank you. To go through it again: you'll have blood drawn now, then the lumbar puncture, and you'll stay with us for monitoring.
Stay overnight? My wife's going to freak out.
I'll call her myself if you'd like. Meanwhile, I'll check in on you again in two hours.
Okay. Thanks, doc.
You did the right thing coming in. The nurse will be with you in a minute.

physical_examination.finding: neck is stiff when I bend your head forward

review_of_systems.details: No confusion, speech or strength problems
